title: Messi scores 99th club goal for Inter Miami, but Nashville seizes late draw
content:
Nashville SC clawed its way to a draw in Miami on Saturday night behind a Sam Surridge brace in a top-of-the-table clash versus Inter Miami. Lionel Messi scored his 99th goal for his MLS club in all competitions, giving Miami a 2-1 lead in the 62nd minute.

Miami and Nashville have become Eastern Conference rivals over the past three seasons. The sides have met in important cup matches, playoffs and high-profile regular-season dates. No team in MLS has conceded more goals to Messi than Nashville. On Saturday, the Argentine scored his 17th goal in 14 games against Nashville.

Still, after a physical match in the humid South Florida weather, the visitors left the Nu Stadium pitch with their heads high. Surridge scored his first goal in the fourth minute, then equalized in stoppage time from close range. The England-born striker delivered a complete performance in a game that Miami desperately wanted to win.

Despite Messi being in pole position to win his third straight MLS MVP award, Miami has been terribly inconsistent this season. Under head coach Guillermo Hoyos, Miami has won just once in its last nine games. Hoyos has symbolized Miami’s lackluster displays.

A close friend of Messi’s, Hoyos has stunted the defending MLS champions’ progression in 2026. Cristian “Kily” González will replace him once the new manager’s work visa is approved.

Nashville, however, has looked and played like the top team in MLS this season. B.J. Callaghan’s team has a 9-point lead over Miami in the Eastern Conference and an 8-point lead over Vancouver in the Supporters’ Shield race.

Surridge scored his 15th goal of the season Saturday. Messi leads the MLS golden boot standings with 19 goals.

Messi, who was nominated this week for the 2026 Ballon d’Or, was dejected with the result. Miami crashed three shots off the post. The third came in the 94th minute after Rodrigo De Paul’s close-range shot nearly gave Miami a last-ditch victory.

In the end, it was another frustrating night for Miami, but one that Nashville may look back on as a pivotal moment in what may be a storybook season.

Nashville won the 2025 U.S. Open Cup, its first trophy since it entered MLS in 2020. Callaghan has since become one of the league’s top coaches and has changed the team’s previous defensive style to a more balanced side with important attacking pieces.

Nashville will host a confident Chicago Fire team on Sept. 19. Miami’s next game is against San Diego FC on Sept. 20 at Nu Stadium.
